name: Sunflower
intro: A sunflower is a tall plant with a big yellow flower. It grows fast in the summer sun.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A sunflower has a tall, straight stem.
The stem is a little bit hairy.
Its leaves are big and rough.
The big flower head is made of hundreds of tiny flowers.
The petals are often yellow, but some are red or orange.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Sunflowers first grew in North America and Mexico.
Now they grow in almost every part of the world.
They do not grow in jungles, deserts, or icy lands.
Farmers grow sunflowers in big fields.
People grow them in gardens too.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A sunflower needs lots of sun.
It likes at least 6 hours of sun each day.
It grows best in rich soil that drains well.
Young plants need soil that stays a little wet.
Bigger plants like a deep drink of water.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A sunflower starts as a seed in the ground.
People plant the seeds after the last frost.
The plant grows very fast in summer.
The flower head opens and blooms in summer.
Each tiny flower can turn into a seed.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Young sunflowers turn to follow the sun.
Grown-up sunflowers mostly face east.
One flower head can hold hundreds of seeds.
Bees visit sunflowers for nectar and pollen.
Kansas is called the Sunflower State.

vocab.meaning: A tiny part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
Tiny flowers that crowd together to make one big flower head.
The dirt that plants grow in.
A sweet juice inside flowers that bees drink.
A yellow dust that flowers need to make seeds.
